name: check
body: clean

name: check
body: clean

name: rubric
rubric: A Brief is written before any research and is the yardstick every later artifact is judged against, so each goal is concrete enough to judge a Dossier by. Its Slides are the spine write-dossier keeps. Fail if a goal is too vague to judge a Dossier against.
body: Learning goal (where AI raises pressure; why clear requirements reduce it) and three step-shaped Actionables are concrete enough to judge a Dossier by; Slides give write-dossier a two-Section spine.

name: rubric
rubric: When the file last changed in substance, with an explicit UTC offset. A `verified` entry counts only while its `at` is at or after this, so an edit re-opens the gate.
body: generated.at 2026-11-10T16:14:32Z: valid datetime with explicit UTC offset (Z).

name: rubric
rubric: Who wrote or last rewrote the file, as an OKF actor: `<producer>/<version>` for an agent (`claude-code/opus-5.5`), `human:<id>` for a person (`human:han`). Fail if an agent-written file names a person, or a file Han edited names an agent.
body: generated.by claude-code/opus-5.5: agent actor for an agent-written copy; Han has not edited the file yet.

name: rubric
rubric: A Brief in Staging is draft; Promotion removes the line when it moves the Brief to src/episodes/<slug>/.
body: status: draft, the allowed value for a Brief in Staging.

name: rubric
rubric: The file name for a reader, equal to the file's h1 so retrieval can list the file by it; the title-matches-h1 check compares them.
body: title 'Why AI relocates the pressure, and why requirements come first' equals the h1 exactly.

name: rubric
rubric: Goals: what the Episode must achieve, stated before it is written.
body: type: brief.

name: rubric
rubric: OKF §5.2 trust: who confirmed the file and when, as a list of `{ by, at }` or one bare mapping (OKF reads a bare mapping as a one-element list). `process:markdown-harness` once the checks pass, `human:han` once Han approves at the gate; an entry counts only while its `at` is at or after generated.at. The shape, actor and datetime are checked in tests/docs/episode-staging.test.ts, because one address cannot govern both the list and the bare mapping.
body: verified absent: correct before checks and reviewer pass; the job writes process:markdown-harness afterwards.

name: rubric
rubric: The sections a Brief must settle, in reading order, so the grill knows what is left and research starts from settled questions. Fail if a section holds what belongs in a different one.
body: Every required section present in order; each holds its own kind of content. Open ideas holds the pipeline note about Style, which is the feedback-loop home for it.

name: rubric
rubric: The working title of the Episode, naming its subject. Fail if it names the Format or a process instead of the subject.
body: h1 names the subject (AI relocating pressure, requirements first), not the Format or a process.

name: rubric
rubric: Foundations, Teardown or Short, and the planned duration; or, for a Brief that is not an Episode, the Resource kind it builds (`guide`) and the planned duration; or, for an Explorable page, `Explorable page`, its slug and its Slides, which have no planned duration. Together they set the scale of everything below. Fail if either is missing.
body: Format names Explorable page, slug software-ecology, and its three Slides (Title, Play, Why/how/what); no duration needed for an Explorable page.

name: rubric
rubric: Who watches, what they already know and what they want, so every later choice can be judged against them. Fail if it names a group without saying what they know or want.
body: Both groups named with what they know (org chart / own task) and what they want (top-down view / zoom out to adjacent roles).

name: rubric
rubric: One line naming a style from docs/design/design-guide.md and the audience reason for it; the designers keep that style for the whole Episode. Fail if it names no style, names none the design guide lists, or gives no audience reason.
body: Names Editorial, listed in design-guide.md; audience reason given (managers lead); meaning colours human/machine/ai used only for their meanings, as Editorial requires.

name: rubric
rubric: What the viewer can do or explain afterwards, in one or two sentences, the end every Section moves towards. Fail if it names a topic to cover instead of a change in the viewer.
body: States a change in the viewer: they can see where AI increases pressure in their org and why clear requirements reduce it.

name: rubric
rubric: Concrete steps a viewer takes after watching, one per item; each is later backed by at least one Slide. Fail if an item is a belief or a topic instead of a step a viewer could take.
body: Three ordered steps a viewer can take (map team and mark narrowest review; check review capacity before speeding a node; write requirement for someone new). Play and Why slides back them.

name: rubric
rubric: The opening that earns the first thirty seconds. Fail if it only announces the topic instead of giving the viewer a reason to stay.
body: Hook leans on a cartoon everyone knows and turns it ('wrong swing built ten times faster'): a reason to stay, not a topic announcement.

name: rubric
rubric: The single line of argument from the hook to the learning goal, which every Section advances. Fail if it lists topics instead of making one argument, or does not end at the learning goal.
body: One argument: system not actors, telephone game, unclear requirements always hurt, AI accelerates and pushes pressure into spec and review, so clearest requirements lower it; ends at the Learning goal.

name: rubric
rubric: Two Threads told in turns so the audience never follows one too long, chosen in the grill by planned duration in any Format.
body: Threads heading absent; optional, so nothing to judge.

name: rubric
rubric: The first Thread, usually the mechanism or argument. Fail if it does not carry the Red thread.
body: No Threads, so no A thread; nothing to judge.

name: rubric
rubric: The second Thread, told in turns with the A thread and strengthening it. Fail if cutting it would not weaken the A thread.
body: No Threads, so no B thread; nothing to judge.

name: rubric
rubric: One everyday picture the Episode returns to, giving the abstract idea a handle; a list keeps the parts of the picture as Han said them. Fail if picturing it takes expertise, or it offers several pictures.
body: One everyday picture, plumbing, with its parts (pipe, valve, pump, clean water, sediment); needs no expertise to picture.

name: rubric
rubric: Story rules every Slide obeys, one per item, so a writing job and its reviewer check each Slide against them. Fail if an item governs a single Slide, which belongs in that Slide's purpose.
body: Four rules, each binding every Slide (AI as accelerator, no blamed role, both sides per node, reusable); none governs a single Slide.

name: rubric
rubric: The spine Han settled: one h3 per Section, each an ordered list of its page Slides, numbered on across Sections. Each item is `**<title>** — <purpose>. _Visual:_ <idea>`, with an optional `_Research:_ <n, m>` naming the research questions it rests on, and a leading `(A)` or `(B)` when the Brief has Threads; the staging test checks that shape. write-dossier keeps this spine. Fail if a purpose advances no step of the Red thread, the Slides take its steps out of argument order, the first Slide does not carry the Hook, or the last Section does not land the Learning goal.
body: Play carries the Hook (opens on the cartoon's Swing step) and runs to AI on; Why/how/what lands the Learning goal incl. clearer requirements lowering pressure; items keep **title** — purpose. _Visual:_ shape.

name: rubric
rubric: A Section, titled as the table of contents names it, holding the page Slides that make one step of the Red thread. Fail if its Slides serve more than one step.
body: Two h3 Sections, each one Slide and one step of the Red thread (play the system; explain why/how/what); titles under 60 chars.

name: rubric
rubric: The questions the Episode's claims depend on, one per item, each researched on its own: a why question scoped to a subject matter. Fail if a question names the Episode, bundles two questions or asks what no claim needs, or a claim elsewhere in the Brief needs a question that is missing.
body: Six single why questions scoped to subject matter; Q3/Q4 split per user's Q10; none names the Episode; each cited by a Slide; Red thread claims (bottleneck shift, unclear reqs, context rot) all covered.

name: rubric
rubric: Files (pdf, word) brought in as a model for the Episode (a deck, a sketch, miro slides export), one per item, `[<title>](reference/<file-slug>/design-reference.md)`: the file the convert-references job writes from the copy at `.scratch/<slug>/<file-slug>.<file-extension>`. Fail if an item names a file the prompt or handoff did not bring.
body: No Episode Design Reference heading; the handoff brought no file.

name: rubric
rubric: Ideas the grill did not settle, kept for the feedback loop; nothing here binds the run. Fail if an item restates or overrides a settled section.
body: Four ideas (Conway's law, per-card animation, landing hero, drop Style) none restates or overrides a settled section.

name: rubric
rubric: The text under every heading except Episode Design Reference is the user's wording: `.scratch/<slug>/handoff.md` when it exists, their answers in this session, or a shape-only fix the Job's summary names.
body: Diff vs handoff.md: only generated, slug (Q1/Q11), Red thread ending (Q8), Section/Format reorder and Visual order (Q9), RQ1 transcript note moved and RQ3 split with refs renumbered (Q10). All recorded user answers.

name: rubric
rubric: No two sections of the Brief contradict each other, and no section contradicts itself.
body: No contradictions: Format's three Slides match Title + two listed Slides; Red thread, Analogy (clean water) and Why slide agree requirements lower pressure; Constraint 'no tool names' honoured after Claude Code left RQ1.

name: rubric
rubric: Every sentence is one a downstream job acts on: a sentence that changes no job's output is noise.
body: Each sentence feeds a job: Audience/Style/Constraints steer writers and designers, Slides/Visual steer the build, RQs steer research, Open ideas feed the feedback loop.
